title: Motor start/stop (jog)
summary: Run the conveyor motor only while Start is held, the way a setter jogs a belt into position. The normally closed Stop button and the overload relay must always win.
objectives: Combine a normally open and a normally closed input with AND
Use a feedback contact to show what really happened
starterProgram:
PROGRAM Main
VAR_INPUT
    StartPB : BOOL; (* Start button S1, normally open: TRUE while pressed. *)
    StopPB : BOOL; (* Stop button S2, normally closed: TRUE while NOT pressed (wire-break safe). *)
    MotorFeedback : BOOL; (* Contactor auxiliary contact: TRUE when the contactor has pulled in. *)
    OverloadOK : BOOL; (* Overload relay contact, normally closed: TRUE while the motor is not overloaded. *)
END_VAR
VAR_OUTPUT
    MotorContactor : BOOL; (* Contactor coil K1: TRUE energizes the motor. *)
    RunLamp : BOOL; (* Green run lamp H1. *)
END_VAR

(* MotorContactor runs while StartPB is held, unless Stop is pressed or the overload tripped. RunLamp shows the contactor feedback. *)

END_PROGRAM
instructions: MotorContactor is TRUE only while Start is held.
Pressing Stop (StopPB becomes FALSE) or an overload (OverloadOK FALSE) switches the motor off even while Start is held.
RunLamp shows the contactor's auxiliary contact MotorFeedback, not the command.
hints: StopPB is TRUE while Stop is NOT pressed, because the button is normally closed.
MotorContactor := StartPB AND StopPB AND OverloadOK;

scenarios.title: Press Stop while Start is held

criteria.title: The motor runs while Start is held
criteria.onFail: MotorContactor did not follow the held Start button.

criteria.title: The motor stops when Start is released
criteria.onFail: The motor kept running after Start was released. A jog must not latch.

criteria.title: Stop overrides a held Start
criteria.onFail: The motor kept running while Stop was pressed.

criteria.title: RunLamp shows the real contactor state
criteria.onFail: RunLamp was off while the contactor was pulled in.
